My LafargeHolcim Bangladesh valuation

Download the model (XLSX)

The model is a separate spreadsheet; this page's tool is a simplified, single-stage version of the same method.

What it does

A normal DCF asks “what is this company worth?”. This tool also runs it backwards: given the share price, it finds the revenue growth the market must be assuming. Comparing that number with the company's history is the quickest check on whether a valuation is realistic.

How it works

Data comes from the company's own XBRL filings via SEC EDGAR: five fiscal years of revenue, operating income, depreciation, capex, working capital, cash, debt, diluted shares and the effective tax rate. Companies tag revenue under different names, so the extractor tries a list of tags in order and reports which one it used.

The forward model is a ten-year free-cash-flow-to-firm DCF with three operating drivers: revenue growth \(g\), operating margin \(m\) and a sales-to-capital ratio \(S\) that converts growth into reinvestment.

$$FCFF_t = R_{t}\, m\,(1-\tau) \;-\; \frac{R_t - R_{t-1}}{S}, \qquad R_t = R_{t-1}(1+g)$$

The discount rate is a weighted average cost of capital from a small CAPM builder:

$$k_e = r_f + \beta \cdot ERP, \qquad WACC = w_e\,k_e + w_d\,k_d\,(1-\tau)$$

After year 10 a Gordon terminal value applies, with terminal growth \(g_T\) capped at the risk-free rate (a company cannot outgrow the economy forever) and with enough reinvestment to fund that growth at a return equal to the WACC:

$$TV_{10} = \frac{NOPAT_{11}\,(1 - g_T/WACC)}{WACC - g_T}, \qquad V_0 = \sum_{t=1}^{10}\frac{FCFF_t}{(1+WACC)^t} + \frac{TV_{10}}{(1+WACC)^{10}}$$

Equity value is enterprise value plus cash minus debt; divide by diluted shares for value per share.

The reverse DCF holds every input except \(g\) fixed and solves \(V_0(g)/\text{shares} = P\) by bisection between −50% and +100% a year. If no growth rate in that range reproduces the price, the tool says so rather than extrapolating.

The heatmap re-runs the model over a grid of growth rates and discount rates and colours each cell by its distance from the market price.

Why I built it

Limits

  • One constant growth rate for ten years is a simplification; real forecasts fade. Use the margin and sales-to-capital sliders to shape the path.
  • XBRL tags are inconsistent across companies. Banks, insurers and REITs do not fit an FCFF model at all; the tool will load them but the output is not meaningful.
  • Operating leases, minority interests, preferred stock and stock-based compensation are not adjusted for.
  • The share price is typed, not fetched, so it can be stale. The date box is there for a reason.
